title: Effectivity of a normalized DVR tower
statement:
For a tower in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], put
$M=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_m M_m$. Then the canonical
counit comparisons give coherent isomorphisms

$$
M\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n
\qquad(n\geq1).
$$

In particular $M$ is derived complete in the sense of
[def-weil-derived-complete]. No constructibility or boundedness
is required for this effectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply the proved finite-comparison theorem at each n with the fixed normalized completed-coefficient adjunction.

source.place: Proof: coefficient triangles, nilpotent fibres, finite free tensor comparison and canonical maps

proof.text: Consecutive arrows in a distinguished Roos triangle compose to zero. Project its middle equation onto coordinate n to get p_(n+1) followed by the successor transition equals p_n. Induct on m-n using localization of evaluation natural transformations to get the same equation for every longer transition and the identity case. Substitute tower_tau, then apply the injective adjunction Hom equivalence. Naturality of the restriction composition isomorphism and the unit formula give exactly the displayed finite-coefficient coherence equation.

source.place: Proof: coefficient triangles, nilpotent fibres, finite free tensor comparison and canonical maps

proof.text: The published normalized adjunction unit on a K-flat representative is the localized ordinary tensor unit. Apply the K-flat quotient model with this unit identity. Use P itself as the representative with identity resolution. Compose each tower evaluation isomorphism with the inverse restricted finite comparison and the K-flat model isomorphism. The coherence equation and the model quotient identity show that these maps intertwine successor transitions. The adjunction unit formula shows that the original limit projections become exactly the canonical integral reduction cone legs. Their products give an isomorphism of the original Roos triangle with the canonical reduction triangle, transferring distinguishedness. This is precisely IsDerivedComplete.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, $T$ a scheme, and $\pi_E\in\{\pi_E,\ell\}$; put
$A_n=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$, so that $(A_n)_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}/\pi_E^n$. Let
$(M_n)_n$ be a tower of complexes $M_n\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)$, given as an
object of the derived category of towers of
[det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], whose reduction maps

$$
M_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_m}A_n\longrightarrow M_n\qquad(m\geq n)
$$

are isomorphisms; this is the normalization condition of
[sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], without its constructibility and boundedness
conditions. Put $M=R\varprojlim_mM_m\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, the
derived limit of [sk-prop-pe-milnor] with each $M_m$ regarded as an
$\mathcal O_{E,T}$-module. Then the canonical maps

$$
M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}A_n\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }M_n
\qquad(n\geq1)
$$

are isomorphisms, compatible with the reduction maps. In particular $M$ is
derived $\pi_E$-complete in the sense of [def-pe-derived-complete], and
$(M_n)_n$ is isomorphic to the tower of reductions of $M$. No
constructibility or boundedness is required for this effectivity assertion.

proof.text:
Fix $n$, and discard the finitely many indices $m<n$.
The coefficient complex

$$
C_{m,n}=A_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_E} A_n
=[A_m\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}A_m]
$$

is in degrees $[-1,0]$. Its augmentation to $A_n$ has
fiber $(\pi_E^{m-n}A_m)[1]\cong A_n[1]$, as an object of
$D(A_m)$, because $\mathcal O_E$ is $\pi_E$-torsion free. This identification uses multiplication by
$\pi_E^{m-n}$; its inverse on the fiber is determined by the
single nonzero cohomology module. For $m'\geq m\geq n$,
coefficient reduction sends the generator $\pi_E^{m'-n}$ to
$\pi_E^{m'-m}\pi_E^{m-n}$. Thus the fiber transition, expressed
in these copies of $A_n[1]$, is multiplication by
$\pi_E^{m'-m}$.

Tensor this coefficient triangle with $M_m$ over $A_m$.
The normalization isomorphisms, which are compatible with composition because
they are induced by the transition maps of one object of the tower category,
give a tower of triangles

$$
M_n[1]\longrightarrow M_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_m} C_{m,n}
\longrightarrow M_n\longrightarrow .
$$

The right-hand tower is constant, with identity transitions. The
left-hand transition for $m'\to m$ is multiplication by
$\pi_E^{m'-m}$: this follows by tensoring the just computed
coefficient map and using the same normalization isomorphisms. The
calculation is made in strict coefficient complexes and their
derived tensor products, so these are compatible triangles of
towers, not independently chosen cones.

Every $n$ successive left-hand transitions compose to zero.
In the defining triangle
$R\varprojlim\to\prod\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod$ of [sk-prop-pe-milnor], the
shift $s$ on the derived product therefore satisfies $s^n=0$.
The inverse of $1-s$ is $1+s+\cdots+s^{n-1}$, so this
fiber tower has zero derived limit. The quotient $A_n$ has
the bounded finite-free $\mathcal O_{E,T}$-resolution
$[\mathcal O_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}]$, and
$M_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}A_n\simeq M_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_m}C_{m,n}$. Tensoring with this resolution commutes
with derived products and fibers, hence with the derived limit
in that triangle. Taking limits in the displayed triangles
now proves

$$
M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}} A_n
\cong R\varprojlim_m(M_m\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}} A_n)
\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n.
$$

Every map is induced by the tower projections and coefficient
augmentations, so these isomorphisms have the stated cocycle.
They identify the original tower with the quotient tower of
$M$; its limit is $M$, so $M$ is derived $\pi_E$-complete
([def-pe-derived-complete]).
For the coefficient tower itself, $(A_n)_T$ with the quotient maps, the
derived limit is $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ in degree zero: the ordinary limit is
$\mathcal O_{E,T}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], and
$R^1\varprojlim$ vanishes because on a weakly contractible quasi-compact
pro-étale basis object sections are exact and the transition maps are
surjective on sections.
